name: two_stage_steam_compressor_intercooling
title: Two-stage compression of superheated steam with intercooling at the optimal intermediate pressure
summary: Superheated steam (0.15 kg/s, 100 kPa to 625 kPa, 100 K superheat) is compressed by a two-stage isentropic compressor with intercooling back to the supply temperature, the intermediate pressure being set by the rule of equal stage pressure ratios (the work-minimising choice for ideal gases, Cengel & Boles). The model compares the powers of the single-stage isentropic, two-stage and isothermal (INTEGRAL of v dP) compressors and of a liquid pump, and computes the heats rejected in the intercooler and by the isothermal compression.

origin.course: Thermodynamique appliquee (ULiege MECA0002), repetition session R04, exercise 2

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file (35 variables), converted with --ees-units (kPa/kJ to Pa/J hand conversion of the model); the native file two_stage_steam_compressor_intercooling.eescode is the verified file
verification.notes: Native file vs EES: 34/34 common variables agree (max 4.47e-6 on W_dot_isoT, 4.2e-6 on Q_dot_cp_isoT2, the others <= 3.4e-6; same water formulation), v_gaz renamed v_liq. The largest deviations are the integral-based quantities: W_dot_isoT is the EES trapezoidal rule with a 1 kPa step (59065.135 W), CoolSolve integrates with RK4 and returns the exact integral of the CoolProp specific volume (59064.871 W, checked with scipy quad). Native file solved with CoolSolve branch fix/library-gaps-2 (CS-GAP-INTEGRAL-LIMITS and CS-BUG-INTEGRAL-FACTOR closed): 525 steps, the 55 common variables equal the former _coolsolve variant (removed) to 12 digits. Optimisation documented and checked: sweep of p_int confirms the equal-ratio intermediate pressure (250 kPa) within 1 kPa / 0.001 % of the true minimum-work optimum of real steam (~251 kPa). CS-GAP-OPTIM stays listed for information (model shipped at the optimum).
